- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; apply a 1-2 day lag correction downward.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days) — adjust upward by 1–3% if sentiment remains bullish.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting — apply a 2–3 day “sentiment catch-up” adjustment.
